newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Senate vote on MMT possible on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Senate vote on MMT possible on Thursday.

text.p: Liberals in the Canadian Senate were pressing for a final vote on Thursday on a government bill that would effectively ban the gasoline additive MMT, a Senate official said on Tuesday.
Ethyl Corp of Virginia makes the additive and would be shut out of the Canadian market if the bill passed.

The Liberal government announced on Tuesday it intended to file a motion the following day that would limit debate and force a vote next time the bill was considered, said the official, an aide to Joyce Fairbairn, the government leader in the Senate.
That vote would likely be on Thursday, he said.
The Senate, Parliament's unelected chamber, is about evenly split between Conservatives and Liberals.

The Conservatives moved on Tuesday that the Senate first ask the Royal Society of Canada to study MMT, methylcyclopentadienyl manganese tricarbonyl, to see if it really damaged the environment and automobile on-board diagnostic systems as its opponents complained.

The government motion to limit debate was due to be considered on Wednesday and the Conservative motion could be voted upon on Wednesday or Thursday. If the government succeeded in its plan, the final vote on the bill would be on Thursday.
Parliament's elected House of Commons has passed the bill. But with elections looming this year, the bill would probably die if it were referred to the Royal Society for study.
Ethyl Corp intended to lay a claim against Canada for US$200 million under the North American Free Trade Agreement if it was banned.
